close_reason: Decided wontfix for the deprecation-alias suggestion. The on_success_update_email API break is real but the recommendation (#[deprecated] type alias OnSuccessUpdateEmailLegacy) is rejected because: (1) the workspace is at 0.x where breaking changes are permitted per the workspace AGENTS.md posture; (2) the .11 fix REVERSES the diff's type choice from HashMap<Id, PatchObject> to HashMap<String, PatchObject> — adding a deprecation alias for the intermediate Id-keyed shape would re-introduce the type-contract violation flagged in .11; (3) downstream consumers in this workspace already use HashMap<String, PatchObject> via jmap-mail-server::mdn.rs's HashMap<String, _>-style maps for not_sent etc., so the cascade is bounded. The CHANGELOG/release-notes capture of breaking changes is a separate concern that should be addressed via the standard release-notes pass, not via in-crate deprecated aliases.
description:
## Caller contract risk: any caller pinned to a previous jmap-mail-types version using the String/Value shape will fail to compile against the new version.

The diff changes \`MdnSendRequest.on_success_update_email\` from:

\`\`\`rust
pub on_success_update_email: Option<HashMap<String, Value>>,
\`\`\`

to:

\`\`\`rust
pub on_success_update_email: Option<HashMap<Id, PatchObject>>,
\`\`\`

This is wire-byte-identical (both \`Id\` and \`PatchObject\` are \`#[serde(transparent)]\`), but it is NOT a non-breaking Rust API change:

- A caller doing \`map.insert(\"e1\".to_string(), json!({...}))\` previously compiled; now it does not (\`String\` is no longer the key type, \`Value\` is no longer the value type).
- A caller pattern-matching on \`Value::Object(...)\` to inspect a returned patch previously worked; now they must call \`patch.as_map()\` to get the inner map.
- A caller doing \`if let Some(map) = req.on_success_update_email\` then iterating with \`for (k, v) in map\` previously got \`(&String, &Value)\`; now they get \`(&Id, &PatchObject)\`.

### Why this matters in 0.x

The workspace is at 0.x and the workspace AGENTS.md \"Git Commit and Push Policy\" / general posture is permissive of breaking changes pre-1.0. So this is allowed. But:

1. Path-dependencies between sibling crates (\`crate-jmap-mail-server\`, \`crate-jmap-mail-client\`) mean a Rust-API break here cascades through callers within this workspace within the same commit. The diff did not include a sibling-sweep — callers may build today only because no sibling crate uses \`on_success_update_email\` directly.

2. The commit message presents the change as part of \"adopt extras-preservation policy\" (an additive policy), but this typed-up change is independent of extras and would be a justifiable standalone refactor. Mixing the two in a single commit makes the API break less visible during review and harder to revert independently.

### Recommendation

For 0.x: at minimum, add a CHANGELOG note (\"BREAKING: \`on_success_update_email\` is now \`HashMap<Id, PatchObject>\`\") so downstream consumers see the change explicitly. If preserving builds is a goal (it is per the workspace's \"caller can pin to ^0.x\" stance in the supplement template), add a deprecated type alias:

\`\`\`rust
#[deprecated(note = \"use HashMap<Id, PatchObject> directly\")]
pub type OnSuccessUpdateEmailLegacy = HashMap<String, Value>;
\`\`\`

For 1.x: include the change in a coordinated breaking-release pass with a documented migration guide.

### Cross-references

- bd JMAP-zx3s.11 (this supplement): the typed shape itself has a separate underspecification problem (\`Id\` can't hold \`#creationId\` per its own contract). The versioning concern here is independent; even with the type-safety story fixed, the API break is still an API break.
title: on_success_update_email type change is a Rust API break (HashMap<String,Value> -> HashMap<Id,PatchObject>) with no deprecation alias
